uncited: It builds on [Greedy face merging](8935-greedy-face-merging.md) by sweeping the volume along principal axes, checking face visibility against neighbors, and greedily expanding exposed faces into maximal quads.

detail: Greedy Meshing / Face Culling generates a static triangle mesh for a voxel chunk by iterating through occupied voxel positions and emitting geometry only for faces that are adjacent to empty space or transparent blocks [S1, S3, S5, unofficial].

The claim states that the algorithm emits geometry for faces adjacent to 'empty space or transparent blocks'. The provided evidence (Sources S1, S3, and S5) confirms that the algorithm iterates through occupied voxels and emits geometry for faces adjacent to 'empty' or 'missing' neighbors (i.e., where no block exists). However, none of the provided sources mention 'transparent blocks' or any logic for handling transparency (e.g., alpha testing, depth sorting, or specific handling for semi-transparent materials). The evidence only supports the 'empty space' part of the condition.
This approach reduces vertex count and draw calls compared to naive voxel rendering by excluding internal faces [S1, S3, unofficial].

The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly describes an algorithm that iterates through blocks and checks for exposed faces (neighbors missing). It only generates geometry (vertices and triangles) for these exposed faces, effectively excluding internal faces where neighbors exist. Source [S3] notes corroborate this by stating the method emits a quad for each face adjacent to an empty voxel. By excluding internal faces, the approach inherently reduces the total number of vertices and triangles (and consequently draw calls, assuming one mesh per chunk or material) compared to a naive approach that would render all faces of all blocks.
